newsitem.title: USA: Simpson Industries to close Mich. plant.
newsitem.headline: Simpson Industries to close Mich. plant.

text.p: Auto parts maker Simpson Industries Inc said Monday it will close its plant in Jackson, Mich., before the end of 1997, a move that will eliminate about 135 jobs.
The company said the closing will result in a pre-tax charge of $4 million, which will be included in its financial results for the third quarter.

Production of transmission and chassis components at the Jackson plant will be transferred to three other facilities, in Edon, Ohio; Fremont, Ind.; and Bluffton, Ind. The Bluffton facility is not unionized.

Simpson Industries said it informed members of the International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers Local 1515 in Jackson of the closing decision following a lengthy review of the plant. It cited an excess of industry capacity for the components and its desire to improve efficiency by consolidating operations.
